desc: Parse input and store operations with original indices.
Compute furthest[p] and op_for_furthest[p] for type 1 ops using a sweep with a max-heap.
Build next_pos and binary lifting table for next_pos to enable fast computation of f(l,r).
For type 2 ops, compute arrays maxR_at_L[l] and minL_at_R[r]. Build a segment tree over minL_at_R to answer "find first R in [l,U] with minL_at_R[R] ≤ l".
Generate candidate intervals (l,r) with their type 2 cost (0,1,2) as described.
Precompute greedy chains for each distinct l appearing in candidates.
For each candidate, compute f(l,r) from the precomputed chain (or via binary lifting) and lower bound.
Sort candidates by lower bound. For each in order, check feasibility (type 2 ops can be chosen disjoint from the type 1 chain). If feasible, record the solution.
If no candidate is feasible, output -1. Otherwise, output the total cost and the chosen operations (1 for type 1, 2 for type 2, 0 otherwise).
Test the solution on all sample inputs and edge cases (N=1, M=1, large N, no type 1 ops, impossible cases) to verify correctness and performance. Fix any issues found.
Optimize code if performance issues arise (e.g., chain precomputation, memory usage for binary lifting table).
Finalize the code and ensure it runs within constraints (N up to 1e6, M up to 2e5).
